② 'knew' is wrong. 'belongs to a class already knew to have this property' — 'knew' is past tense of 'know'. This structure requires the passive past participle 'known' (as in 'a class already known to...'). Active 'knew' makes no grammatical sense here.

④ 'serve' is wrong. 'Mathematical calculation ability serve as a key indicator' — the subject 'Mathematical calculation ability' is singular (an uncountable noun phrase), so the verb must be singular 'serves', not plural 'serve'.

③ 'having' is wrong. 'belongs to a class already known to having this property' — after 'known to', a bare infinitive (to-infinitive) is required: 'known to have', not 'known to having'. Gerund 'having' cannot follow 'to' in this infinitive structure.

③ 'similar' is wrong. 'We reason similar in everyday life' — 'similar' is an adjective but it modifies the verb 'reason', requiring an adverb. Correct: 'similarly' (adverb). ①abstraction (noun - correct), ②together (adverb - correct), ④have (modal complement - correct).

① 'scatter' is wrong. 'aim to scatter them together and study them all at the same time' — 'scatter together' is self-contradictory. Scatter means to spread apart, which is the opposite of grouping 'together'. Passage uses 'cluster' (묶다).

② 'undermines' is wrong. 'this undermines that every object within a class has a particular property' — 'undermines' means weakens/reduces. The passage says clustering guarantees (assures) properties for all objects. Undermines is the opposite of guarantees.

③ 'collectively' is wrong. 'instead of studying each object collectively' — the purpose of clustering is to study all objects together (collectively). Studying 'each object collectively' is contradictory — 'each' implies individually. Passage says 'individually' (each one separately, which is the inefficient way they avoid).

③ 'deviates' is wrong. 'prove instead that it deviates to a class already known to have this property' — 'deviates to' is ungrammatical (deviate from, not to), and meaning is wrong. The proof strategy is to show the object belongs (is a member of) the class, not deviates from it.

This extends the guarantee beyond already-known objects.
